key_insight: A superconducting soliton-based DAC can convert a simple control pulse into nanosecond-scale flux gates for transmons, enabling fast and robust phase control.
engineering_relevance: This architecture offers CMOS-controllable, multiplexed quantum gate delivery with reduced control-noise sensitivity, making it attractive for scalable quantum hardware.
method: Transduce a trapezoidal drive pulse into a superconducting soliton.
Store the soliton in a DAC load loop to generate controlled flux output.
Use the flux to drive a mutually coupled transmon or gate coupler, with timing set by soliton hold time or a DC-tunable coupler.
evidence_signal: The prototype demonstrated 5.6 ns S-gates with 0.05% per-gate excitation probability, and simulations matched measurements while indicating lower excitation with stronger JJ overdamping.
watch_item: Scaling may be limited by non-local DAC-induced phase errors from high-frequency electromagnetic interference, even on qubits not directly connected to the DACs.
paper_title: Transmon Phase Gates Controlled by Superconducting Soliton DAC
